decision_passages: Peptide therapeutics offer great promise in drug discovery, yet the accurate identification of peptide toxicity remains essential for both safety assessment and biodefense. We developed ToxMamba, a toxic peptide prediction framework that integrates ISM (implicit structural model)-derived pretrained embeddings, state space models (SSMs), multi-scale feature learning, and ensemble voting. Built upon the Mamba architecture, ToxMamba enables efficient sequence modeling and captures contextual patterns across multiple receptive fields from parallel branches. On independent test datasets, ToxMamba consistently surpasses existing methods, improving the F1 score and MCC, by 3.9%-31.7% and 7.5%-46.9% , respectively. Ablation analyses further demonstrate that Mamba-based variants outperformed Transformer, CNN_LSTM_Attention, and KAN architectures across all evaluation metrics. Feature visualization shows that ISM embeddings yielded clearer separation between toxic and non-toxic peptides in the latent space. Intermediate-layer feature analysis identifies key residue-level decision sites associated with toxicity-related functional motifs, supporting the biological interpretability of ToxMamba. Overall, this study provides an efficient and interpretable computational framework for high-throughput toxic peptide screening.

ToxMSRC is a deep learning model for peptide toxicity prediction that integrates multi-scale convolutional neural networks, bidirectional long short-term memory, and residual connections. The model was trained using 1,818 positive samples and 4,569 negative samples, with the positive samples balanced to 3,636 through SMOTE. It achieved favorable performance on two independent test sets. Peptide toxicity is a critical concern in the development of peptide-based therapeutics, as toxic peptides can cause severe side effects, including organ damage, immune reactions, and cytotoxicity. Accurately predicting peptide toxicity is therefore essential to ensure the safety and efficacy of these drugs. Consequently, we developed the ToxMSRC model to improve the prediction accuracy of peptide toxicity and support future advances in medical drug therapy.
